question: Should OpenClaw define a single memory contract that coordinates backend selection, active memory plugin ownership, and automatic memory flush behavior, or should the remaining work be split entirely into narrower role-slot and memory-CRUD issues?
rationale: The remaining change would add or reshape public config, plugin ownership, docs, and migration behavior; source inspection shows the problem is real, but code cannot safely choose the product/API contract.

options.title: Keep Broad Contract Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open as the broad memory-consistency tracker while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42651 settle narrower implementation slices.

options.title: Fold Into Role-Slot Work
options.body: Declare https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60572 the canonical direction and close this issue only after its role-slot PR also documents the backend and flush semantics.

options.title: Document Existing Knobs Only
options.body: Leave the architecture unchanged and improve docs/doctor guidance for `memory.backend`, `plugins.slots.memory`, and `agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush`, accepting that teams must align config manually.

recommendation.title: Keep Broad Contract Tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the broad memory-consistency tracker while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42651 settle narrower implementation slices.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blame and recent memory/plugin-boundary history make steipete the best visible owner for the product/API contract decision.
